text:
maria (support): FYI customer acme-infra is seeing a spike of 5xx/timeouts on the hosted API since ~09:12 UTC. They report ~15% of requests returning 502/504 and lots of latency spikes. They say it started right after a batch of traffic ramped this morning.

acme-infra (customer): seeing 502s from /v1/generate, errors look like `upstream returned error` and sometimes `504`. Entire app degraded. Can you confirm?

maria (support): I grabbed a few logs from the API gateway and runtime. Notable lines:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] runtime: request id=abc123 route=/v1/generate status=502 err="cache read timeout" cache_key="user:prefix:abc"
[2026-03-15T09:12:35Z] kv: GET shard=redis-prod-3 key=user:prefix:abc err="i/o timeout"
[2026-03-15T09:12:36Z] gateway: upstream timeout after=30000ms
```

alex (sre): I can see elevated Redis READ latencies and a lot of connection errors to redis-prod-3 around that time from metrics. Memory/eviction metrics show eviction spikes too. Could be an eviction/compaction/latency storm.

jia (eng-runtime): The runtime treats prefix/KV cache reads as a quick fast-path; if a read hangs beyond 200ms we risk blocking token streaming and downstream timeouts. We do have a circuit-breaker that should short-circuit after X failures — need to confirm thresholds.

kyle (ops): Pinged redis-ops team. Redis cluster showed transient failover on shard 3 at 09:11:58 UTC and a network flapping event between redis-3 and frontend nodes. Reconnects caused client pools to exhaust.

redis-ops-bot: Alert: redis-prod-3 experienced 2x master failovers in 5m, avg read latency 1.2s, client_conn_exhausted=true.

maria (support): Customer asked for repro steps so they can validate. I suggested a minimal curl to reproduce:
```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"short prompt","model":"gpt-redwood-1","max_tokens":64}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | jq -r '.error'
```
They got `upstream timeout` consistently when the issue was at peak.

alex (sre): Immediate mitigation options we discussed:
- flip cache reads to fast-fail (tune runtime to treat cache timeout as miss)
- route affected customers off the problematic shard (route by customer prefix)
- increase gateway timeout temporarily (not ideal)
- scale redis replicas and increase connection pool limits

jia (eng-runtime): We can push a config toggle to treat cache read > 150ms as miss and skip waiting. That is a safe fast rollback — will reduce 5xx risk but might increase tokens/cost for the customer (no cache hit).

kyle (ops): Starting an emergency remediation: restarting redis-proxy on nodes that show excessive TIME_WAIT to free connections, and bumping maxclients on redis-prod-3. Also adding extra fallback memcached abort path. ETA ~7-10m.

maria (support): I communicated to customer: "We're investigating a transient Redis shard issue causing cache reads to time out. We're applying a fallback so reads will short-circuit and your traffic should recover shortly. We'll follow up with postmortem and mitigations. Apologies for the disruption."

acme-infra (customer): thanks. Can you confirm if data loss is possible? We need to know for compliance.

alex (sre): Short answer: no data loss expected for model state; cache is ephemeral. We are not seeing writes lost on persistent stores. This is KV/prefix caching only.

[09:22 UTC] kyle (ops): Applied temporary runtime flag: REDWOOD_CACHE_READ_TIMEOUT_MS=150 and REDWOOD_CACHE_FAIL_OPEN=true for hostpool serving acme-infra. Observed error rate drop from 14% -> 1.5% over next 4 minutes.

maria (support): Customer confirmed recovery: "Errors went away after ~5m, back to normal. We'll monitor and ping if we see anything else. Thanks for the quick response." :thumbsup:

jia (eng-runtime): Root cause hypothesis: a combination of network flaps plus aggressive eviction led to a burst of long tail read latencies on redis-prod-3. Client connection pools got exhausted, and the runtime's synchronous cache read path amplified head-of-line blocking, causing gateway timeouts.

alex (sre): Action items (short):
- postmortem with timeline and RCA (owner: alex)
- tune runtime to async/timeout cache lookups and ensure fail-open by default for hosted API (owner: jia)
- add pool backpressure metrics and early OOM alerts for redis nodes (owner: kyle)
- add automated traffic steering away from degraded shards (owner: alex)

maria (support): I'll send the customer a summary + next steps and attach this thread.

acme-infra (customer): appreciate the transparency and quick mitigation. Please share the postmortem when ready.

jia (eng-runtime): Will follow up with a config PR and planned rollout. Also adding integration test to simulate upstream cache flaps to avoid regressions.

alex (sre): Closing incident in support channel, will open formal incident in /incidents with full timeline and RCA when complete.

kyle (ops): Noting follow-ups: increase default connection pool size per shard, lower default cache read timeout, add a small token-bucket on cache read retries.

maria (support): Marking thread resolved for now. Reopen if customer reports recurrence.

-- end of thread --
